register.privacy: We store only the nickname, age group, settings, lesson results and technical reports of app errors (browser, error text; at most 180 days). Visit counter: the day and a salted hash of the IP address (no address, no link to an account), kept permanently as statistics (the salt is deleted after the month, then a record cannot be tied to an address). In the CW Chat other signed-in users see your nickname and status (in the app, in the room, in a contact) – adults never see minors; only your list of blocked users is stored, keying is not. No e-mail, no health data. You can download or delete your data at any time in the Account tab.

fatigue.whyAcc: For over a minute your accuracy has been {pp} points lower than at the start of the session.

fatigue.noteEndAcc: Towards the end of the lesson your accuracy dropped compared with the start of the session – possibly fatigue. Take a break before the next lesson.
fatigue.noteThirdTtr: Towards the end of the lesson your reaction slowed down by {pct} % – possibly fatigue. Take a break before the next lesson.

verdict.confirm: Excellent, {pct} %! The character "{ch}" will be confirmed in the next session (in {h} h or tomorrow) – memory consolidates it over a break and sleep. Then the next character is added.
verdict.advance: Excellent! {pct} % in the last {n} characters. The next lesson adds the character "{ch}".
verdict.full: Excellent! {pct} % – you have the whole set.
verdict.few: Adding a character needs at least {n} characters in a lesson (now {trials}).
verdict.acc: Adding a character needs {need} % in the last {n} characters (now {pct} %). Continue with the same set – a plateau is normal.
verdict.ttrUnstable: {pct} % overall, but your reaction slowed down towards the end ({slower} %). The character is added once the reaction is stable – try again after a break.
verdict.newFew: {pct} % overall, but the new character "{ch}" sounded only {n}× ({need}× needed). Try a longer lesson.
verdict.newAcc: {pct} % overall, but the new character "{ch}" only {acc} % ({need} % needed). Practise it some more.
verdict.newSlow: {pct} % overall, but you react more slowly to the new character "{ch}" ({ttr} ms, others {others} ms). Practise it some more so that you recognise it instantly.
result.gapEase: Part of the lesson ran with longer gaps (accuracy dropped below 75 %) – that is fine, the coach gives you more time to recognise characters.
result.slowDay: Today you react {pct} % slower than usual on the same characters – probably tiredness. A short lesson or sleep helps more than long training; tomorrow will be better.
result.fluency: Fluency block: {pct} % at {wpm}/{fwpm} WPM (not counted in the result).
result.fluencyTtr: Fluency block: {pct} % at {wpm}/{fwpm} WPM, reaction {ttr} ms (not counted in the result).

result.warmupOk: – that is how well you remember the characters.
result.loadDayWarn: Already {min} min today. More than {max} min a day adds little – better continue tomorrow.
result.loadSessionEnd: The session has lasted {min} min – after {max} min concentration drops. I suggest stopping; what you learned consolidates over a break and sleep.

dash.accNote: The coach keeps the lesson accuracy around 85 %, so do not expect a steady rise here – progress shows in characters and reaction.
dash.ttrNote: ms from the end of the character to the key press – lower is better. After a character is added it usually rises for a while.
dash.warmTip: warm-up {warm}, end of the previous session {prev}
dash.warmNote: Accuracy in the first 90 s of a session – the best measure of what you remember over a break and sleep.
dash.copyAccNote: Copy-behind lessons. The ladder step goes up after 2 sessions ≥ 90 %, after 2 sessions below 75 % it gets easier.
dash.lagNote: How many characters behind the sender you type. A longer and stable lag is the goal – your head holds more characters, in U4 whole words.

about.title: About
about.intro: A free trainer for receiving and sending Morse code. Author: OK2MTW.
about.licence: The app is free software under the licence EUPL-1.2 (European Union). You may use, study, modify and distribute it free of charge. If you make a modified version available to other people (even just over a network), you must make its source code available under the same licence.
about.morsePro: © Stephen C. Phillips – text to Morse conversion and timing (WPM, Farnsworth). EUPL-1.2. github.com/scp93ch/morse-pro, author of the website morsecode.world.
about.methodText: The Koch method (Ludwig Koch, 1936) and the character order of LCWO.net (Fabian Kurz, DJ5CW); Farnsworth timing; instant character recognition (ICR) training after morsecode.world and CWops CW Academy; findings on differences between learners (Long Island CW Club). We do not take over texts and content of these projects – only principles.
about.contentSources: Abbreviations and prefixes after the exam questions of the Czech Telecommunication Office CTU (06/2025); the selection of Q codes and their meanings after the Q-kodex of the Czech Radio Club. Texts are in our own words.
demo.title: Try it – three characters
demo.text: A short beginner lesson with the characters K, M and U, about a minute. You hear a character and answer by tapping the keyboard below (on a PC also with the keyboard). Nothing is saved.
demo.sound: Turn the sound on; headphones are best.
demo.noAudio: Sound could not be started – try again.
demo.listen: This is how this character sounds ({i}/{n})
demo.noAnswers: No answers – never mind, try again.
demo.reaction: Typical reaction {ms} ms after the end of the character
demo.more: In real training the coach adds characters one by one, adjusts the pace and watches for fatigue, and your progress is saved. Accounts are created by invitation only.
demoBand.title: This is how the band sounds
demoBand.text: The goal of the training: understand a real contact even in noise and interference. Listen to a sample – the text appears exactly when a character has sounded (in training you do not see it, of course, you write it yourself).
demoBand.goal: The training leads here step by step: from two characters through the whole alphabet, words and abbreviations to a contact in interference. The coach watches your pace and fatigue. Accounts are by invitation only for now.
news.title: What's new
news.i18n: The app now speaks English too. Switch the language in the menu under the user icon → Settings → Language; it applies to your other devices as well.
news.demo: Demo without an account: the login page has a “Try it” tab – a one-minute lesson with three characters. Feel free to send the link to friends so they can try Morse code.
news.extraChars: The main programme now has 44 characters. The rare punctuation , ' : ) " @ ! is hardly used in amateur radio – it is an optional extension you can turn on in Settings → “Learn the extension too”. The prosigns KN, AS, BT and AR stay in the main programme.
news.earlyCopy: You can try copy behind before level U3: from 10 mastered characters Home shows a “Copy behind (trial)” card – groups from your characters only. Character lessons stay the main thing; copy behind starts fully at U3 and continues where you stop.

band.title: Band sound (listening test)
band.settingsHint: In development: noise, fading, interference and real keying – coaches only. Nothing is stored.
band.intro: Pick a situation and listen. Judge whether it sounds like a real band – what is overdone, what is missing, what disturbs unnaturally. The text is a random QSO line, you do not need to copy it.
band.adjustHint: Changes apply from the next line.
band.presetHint.clean: As in the lessons – for comparison.
band.presetHint.weak: A station just above the noise, 500 Hz filter.
band.presetHint.qsb: The signal slowly fades out and comes back (short-wave fading).
band.presetHint.flutter: Fast strength variation, typical of polar paths.
band.presetHint.qrn: Atmospheric discharges – short crashes, mostly in summer on the lower bands.
band.presetHint.qrm: Two more stations close to the frequency, wide 2400 Hz filter – you hear them all.
band.presetHint.qrmNarrow: The same interference with a narrow 250 Hz filter – neighbours get weaker.
band.presetHint.hand: Irregular dot and dash lengths as with a straight key, harder edge.
band.presetHint.chirp: The tone “chirps” at key-down and the whole transmission slowly drifts – an older transmitter.
band.presetHint.evening: Everything at once, mildly: noise, fading, static, two stations, hand keying.

home.headDesc: A QSO is played once – type nothing, just listen and remember. Then write its key data (call, RST, name, QTH…). Now: {name}.
home.headMobile: You answer with the normal phone keyboard, without a time limit.
head.pauseHint: An interrupted QSO is not scored. Lesson time is stopped.
head.verdictMid: {acc} correct answers – a good zone for learning. The next step comes from 90 % in 2 sessions.
head.verdictLow: {acc} – hard for now. Never mind: listen to the whole QSO and repeat the data in your mind; a step back comes by itself after 2 sessions below 75 %.
head.short: A session counts for progress from {n} questions.
headResult.title: Head-copy lesson result
news.head: Head copy (U6): a QSO is played once, nothing is typed, then you write its key data – call, RST, name, QTH. As a trial from level U4 on the Copy screen, the whole ladder (30–45 WPM, also on the band) from U5; 40 WPM without interference leads to level U6 Master.

entry.title: Entry test – I already know CW
entry.cardText: Every character is played twice in random order, you answer on the keyboard. The test suggests how many characters to start with, so you do not begin with K M.
entry.settingsHint: Already know CW? The entry test finds out which characters you know.
entry.howTo: Type every character you hear. Nothing is corrected during the test – if you do not know, just wait (6 s).
entry.result: You know {known} of {n} characters (both tries correct within {ms} ms). In the Koch order the first {level} in a row.
entry.resultNext: Lessons start there – the next new character will be {ch}.
entry.resultAll: You have the whole main programme – the coach takes you to full speed and then to copy behind.
entry.unsure: Unsure or slow: {list} – they come one by one as new characters (with an introduction).
entry.keepHigher: Back to Home (you already have {n} characters)
news.entry: Entry test for those who already know CW: every character twice, the app suggests how many characters to start with (on Home for returning operators, otherwise in Settings).
key.title: Telegraph key (experimental)
key.settingsHint: Sending with the HW key CwKey (USB): transcript, analysis, sending exercise, key firmware. Without the HW key you cannot send.
key.outHint: The decoder learns your rhythm from the neighbouring elements (dot and dash lengths and the gaps inside characters, between characters and words) – you do not have to keep the set tempo. Fix a mistake with 7 or more dots – it erases the word in progress, or the word just finished.
key.diag.title: How the decoder reads
key.diag.hint: The last words gap by gap, in dots of your key. Inside a character the key keeps 1 dot; between letters you should leave about 3, between words about 7. Gaps marked with ⚠ are close to a threshold.
key.diag.head: Dot {dot} ms (≈ {wpm} WPM) · letter from {split} dots · word from {word} dots
key.diag.empty: Nothing yet – key a few words.
key.diag.copyFail: No clipboard – select the list above and copy it.
key.rec.hint: Keying is recorded for tuning the decoder automatically (after 20 s of silence or when you leave the page). If you like, also write what you sent and send it – such a record is the most valuable for tuning.
key.rec.placeholder: What you sent, e.g. CQ TEST
key.rec.sent: Sent, thanks. Press Clear the transcript for another attempt.
key.rec.fail: Could not send – try again (the recording waits in the queue).
key.typeHint.hw: A key with its own keyer and buzzer (USB keyboard): the key forms the dots and dashes, the app only reads the stream key (default F13), decodes and evaluates. The speed and swapping the paddles are set on the key (KEY button) and the key makes the sidetone – it is off in the app (can be switched on below). Keys go only to the window with the focus: tap the page before sending.
key.learnStream: Press and release a paddle of the key… (Esc = cancel)
key.estimateHw: Key tempo: ≈ {wpm} WPM (measured from the dots)
key.learnHeld: Capturing… release the paddle and wait a moment.
key.logHint: Time from the first event and the gap to the previous one in ms (browser timestamp). Shows lost and doubled events and the spread; the converter delay is measured with an oscilloscope.
key.logSum.head: Summary: {n} events in {s} s
key.logSum.err: Errors: keydown without keyup {dup}, keyup without keydown {orphan}, held at the end {open}
key.logCopied: Copied to the clipboard (summary + all events).
key.logCopyFail: The clipboard is not available – the text is below, select and copy it.
send.ex.intro: Tasks from the characters for sending ({n}); a series of {tasks} tasks. Nothing is stored yet.
send.ex.wait: After sending wait a moment (about 2 s), or Done (Enter).
send.ex.review: The task above, what was read from your sending below.
send.focus.good: All within the target range – this task is right.
send.focus.ratio.low: Dashes were only {v}× longer than dots (target 3×) – hold the dash longer.
send.focus.ratio.high: Dashes were {v}× longer than dots (target 3×) – release the dash sooner.
send.focus.inGap.low: Gaps between elements inside a character were short ({v}× dot, target 1×) – the elements run together.
send.focus.inGap.high: Gaps between elements inside a character were long ({v}× dot, target 1×) – the character may split in two.
send.focus.charGap.low: Gaps between characters were short ({v}× dot, target 3×) – characters run together; wait a moment after each one.
send.focus.charGap.high: Gaps between characters were long ({v}× dot, target 3×) – they may sound like word gaps.
send.focus.wordGap.low: Gaps between words were short ({v}× dot, target 7×) – words run together.
send.focus.wordGap.high: Gaps between words were long ({v}× dot, target 7×).
send.focus.stability: The tempo varied ({v} %, target up to 15 %) – try a little slower and evenly.

users.offline: User management needs a connection to the server.
users.cwMinor: child – only with group and coach
users.cwMinorGroup: child – room with group and coach

visits.hint: Different visitors per day, in brackets never logged in (someone just found the page). Only a salted hash of the address is stored (the salt is deleted after the month), kept permanently.
visits.total: Different visitors in 14 days: home {lan}, outside {pub} (each once per month).
users.cwKidsHint: (students under 18 you invited: they see classmates of the same group and you; off by default)
users.cwHint: Under “Edit” you can switch the room off for a single student. Adults see adults and coaches, never children.
groups.title: Groups
groups.hint: Deleting a group keeps its students, they only remain without a group.
groups.deleteConfirm: Delete group {name}? Its students ({n}) stay, only without a group.
cw.title: CW room
cw.hint: Pick a user who has the app open (there is a Knock button by the name) and knock. Someone outside the room hears the knock and sees a mark on the CW tab. Once they accept, you are connected: like on the band, one sends, the other listens.
cw.serverBusy: The server is busy right now, the room comes back in a moment.
cw.needsUpdate: The room is not on the server yet – try again after the app update.
cw.offline: No connection to the server – retrying…
cw.noAccess.off: Your coach or the administrator switched the CW room off for you.
cw.noAccess.kids: Your coach has not switched on the room for children yet.
cw.notice.declined: {nick} is not taking a connection now.
cw.voSub: A practice QSO – any time, only in your browser
vo.title: Virtual operator
vo.hint: A practice QSO with a virtual radio amateur. It runs only in your browser: nobody else hears it and nothing is stored. You key with the HW key; the operator answers on the band.
vo.modeHint.quick: Calls, RST, name, QTH, 73 and SK – like a usual short QSO.
vo.modeHint.chatty: Plus 2–4 topics: rig, antenna, power, weather, age, QSL. Ask e.g. RIG? or WX? and it answers.
vo.runHint: Call CQ (CQ CQ DE your call K) or call the operator by its call sign. End every over with K – the operator answers after a short pause. AGN or ? = again, QRS / QRQ = slower / faster. Fix a mistake with 7 dots. Keying while it sends stops it after the word.
vo.heardNothing: The operator understood nothing – try slower and with longer gaps.
vo.tolHint.auto: Now: {v} – by the step of the sending lessons (characters and groups = high, words and QSO = medium).
vo.tolHint.high: The operator joins up to 3 pieces into a known word (QR S → QRS, Q R Q → QRQ, OK2 MTW → the call) and splits words keyed together (QRSK → QRS K). Wrong characters are not corrected.
vo.tolHint.mid: The operator joins 2 pieces into a known word (QR S → QRS) and splits words keyed together (QRSK → QRS K). Wrong characters are not corrected.
vo.tolHint.off: The operator reads exactly what the decoder read – the gaps must be right.
vo.h.name: name {v}
vo.done: The QSO is over – 73! Next: New QSO.
vo.linked: You are connected with another user – the virtual operator after that connection ends.
cw.blockConfirm: Block {nick}? You will stop seeing each other in the room. You can unblock below in the list of blocked users.
cw.rowNotInRoom: {nick} does not have the app open now. You can knock once they open it.
cw.rowLinked: {nick} is in a connection with someone else now.
cw.rowSelfLinked: You are in a connection – end it first.
cw.rowKnocking: You are already knocking on someone else – cancel that first.
cw.bellTitle: Knock Knock – {nick} is knocking in the CW room
cw.keyHintHw: HW keyer: key with the paddles of your key (the key plays the sidetone). Keys only reach the window with the focus. Your over ends after a short silence.
cw.bandHint: Only you hear your choice; the other station chooses their own. A weak noise always stays.
news.vo: Virtual operator in the CW Chat: the first entry of the list. A practice QSO any time – call CQ or its call sign and it answers on the band. Two kinds: a quick QSO (RST, name, QTH) and a chatty radio amateur (rig, antenna, weather…). It understands AGN, QRS and QRQ. It runs only in your browser.
news.hwOnly: Sending is now with the HW key CwKey (USB) only – the on-screen key and the keyboard paddles are gone. The Key page has "How the decoder reads": gap by gap in dots of your key. Fix a mistake with 7 dots.
news.cwRoom: CW room: the “CW Chat” tab shows who is in the app. Knock at a user in the room (Knock Knock) and once they accept, you send to each other with the on-screen key or the keyboard – like on the air, with noise and interference of your choice.
cw.showRx: Transcript of what I received (after each over)
fw.title: CwKey firmware
fw.available: Firmware {version} is ready on the server (released {date}).
fw.none: The server has not downloaded any firmware yet (it checks GitHub once a day).
fw.installedUnknown: Nothing written from this device yet – the app does not know the version in the key (FW 0.3.0 cannot tell it).
fw.offer: Firmware {version} is available for the connected key. Update?
fw.step1: Connect the key with a USB cable and press NRST on the module twice quickly (within half a second). A drive STMF411BOOT (F411) or BlackPill (F401) appears and the LED glows.
fw.step2pick: Select that drive (its top folder) and allow editing. The app recognises the chip, checks the file and writes it.
fw.step2manual: This browser cannot write to the drive. Choose the chip (written on the module), download the checked file and copy it to the drive (Android: the Files app, the key on an OTG cable).
fw.after: The key restarts by itself (the drive disappears, a warning about removing it is fine). Then one long LED blink and the paddles key again – press one to confirm.
fw.checking: Chip {mcu}: downloading and checking the file…
fw.downloaded: The file {file} is downloaded and checked. Copy it to the drive {drive}, then confirm.
fw.keyBack: The key with firmware {version} keys again ✓
fw.err.pick: The drive could not be opened. Try again, or download the file and copy it by hand.
fw.err.notDrive: The folder {name} is not the key's bootloader drive (no INFO_UF2.TXT). Press NRST twice and select the drive STMF411BOOT or BlackPill.
fw.err.download: The file could not be downloaded from the server.
fw.err.sha: The downloaded file does not match its checksum – nothing was written.
fw.err.uf2: The file does not have the right form for the key (it could damage the bootloader) – nothing was written.
fw.err.write: Writing failed. Check that the key drive is still connected and try again.
fw.midiOn: Read the version from the key over USB MIDI (firmware 0.4.0 and newer, on trial)
fw.midi.unsupported: This browser has no MIDI (Chrome or Edge on a computer and Chrome on Android do). The version is still what this device wrote last.
fw.midi.noPort: I cannot see the key over MIDI – is it connected? Firmware 0.3.0 has no MIDI; that one is updated the old way (NRST twice).
fw.midi.denied: MIDI access is not allowed. Allow it in the site settings (the icon left of the address) and turn the switch on again.
fw.midi.reading: Reading the version from the key…
fw.midi.noAnswer: The key did not answer over MIDI.
fw.inKey: The key runs firmware {version} (chip {chip}) – read over MIDI.
fw.bootHint: Or let the app switch the key to the bootloader over MIDI (do not key meanwhile):
fw.bootBtn: Switch the key to the bootloader
fw.boot.ok: The key is switching to the bootloader – its drive appears in a moment. Go on with the next step.
fw.boot.busy: The key is keying or holds PTT – release the paddles and try again.
fw.boot.err: The key did not switch to the bootloader. Use NRST twice.
key.noKey: Connect the HW key CwKey (USB) and press a paddle.
key.noKeyHint: Sending needs the HW key: it forms the dots and dashes itself, the app reads and decodes them. Without the key you can still listen and train receiving. A new key or a key that does not respond: the CwKey firmware card below and the key manual.
cw.noKey: Connect the HW key CwKey (USB) to send – without it you only listen. More on the Key page.
vo.keyTempo: My QRS / QRQ changes the speed of my key too (USB MIDI)
vo.keyTempoHint: The key slows down or speeds up by the same step as the operator. The KEY button on the key has priority. After the QSO the key goes back to its speed.
vo.key.hand: Key changed with the button: {wpm} WPM
vo.key.err: Could not change the speed of the key
news.fw: Firmware of the CwKey key right from the app: the Key page → Firmware offers a new version and guides you through the upload (Chrome on a computer writes straight to the key's drive). With FW 0.4.0 or newer and USB MIDI on, the app reads the version from the key and switches it to the bootloader without the button.
news.keyTempo: Virtual operator: when you send QRS or QRQ, your key can slow down or speed up too (an option in the QSO settings, USB MIDI only). The KEY button has priority; after the QSO the key goes back to its speed.
send.lesson.title: Sending lesson
send.lesson.state: step {i} of {n}: {step} · {k} of {need} lessons ≥ 90 % in a row
send.lesson.offline: Could not load the lessons (no connection to the server). The exercise below works anyway.
send.lesson.qsoWait: QSO sentences need all letters and digits among the characters for sending – until then you send words from the characters you have set.
send.lesson.about.char: Single characters you can already receive. Two lessons in a row with at least 90 % correct move you on.
send.lesson.about.group: Groups of 5 characters – keep the gaps between characters even.
send.lesson.about.word: Words from the characters you know – the gap between words is longer than between characters (7 : 3).
send.lesson.about.qso: Sentences as in a QSO: CQ, RST, name, QTH, 73.
send.lesson.up: Lesson saved – you move on to the next step: {step}.
send.lesson.saved.ok: Lesson saved · {k} of {need} lessons ≥ 90 % in a row.
send.lesson.saved.queued: The lesson will be saved when the server is reachable.
send.habit.wordShort: Habit of the hand: the gap between words is almost the same as between characters – wait longer between words (norm 7 : 3).
send.habit.charLong: Habit of the hand: the gaps between characters are long – start the next character sooner (norm 3 dots).
send.habit.paddle: Habit of the hand: characters have one element more or less – probably the paddle (released late or an unreliable return).
ca.title: Certificate of the home network
ca.why: To install the app in the home network, the phone must trust the certificate of this installation (once).
ca.step1: Android: Settings, Security (and privacy), More security settings, Encryption and credentials.
ca.step2: Install a certificate, CA certificate, confirm the warning and pick the downloaded file. A screen lock is needed.
ca.step3: Close Chrome completely, open this address again and install the app from the menu.
ca.familyLink: Family Link (a child's phone): a parent may block installing certificates. Then use the address outside the home network – it works there without a certificate.
news.v1: Version 1.0.0: the trainer now covers receiving (U1–U6, vocabulary) and sending – the HW key CwKey, CW Chat with knocking and 1 : 1 contacts, the virtual operator and trainer groups. Thanks to everyone who tested!
news.sendLessons: Sending lessons on the Key page: characters → groups → words → QSO sentences. Two lessons in a row with at least 90 % correct move you on; the summary says what to focus on and names the habits of the hand.
news.voTol: The virtual operator tolerates inexact gaps by your sending level: it reads “QR S” as QRS and “QRSK” as QRS K. Wrong characters are not corrected. Set it in CW Chat → Virtual operator → Tolerance of gaps.
send.ownHint: Characters and tempo of sending are independent of receiving – they may be ahead or behind. The first time they were taken from receiving.
settings.themeHint.system: Follows the setting of the phone or computer. Applies to this device only.
settings.themeHint.light: Always a light background. Applies to this device only.
settings.themeHint.dark: Always a dark background. Applies to this device only.
settings.themeHint.sun: Light by day, dark at night – today sunrise {rise}, sunset {set} (approximately for the Czech Republic). Applies to this device only.
news.sendMenu: Sending has its own item in the main menu. Characters and tempo of sending are set separately – independent of receiving.
news.theme: Settings are split into collapsible topics. New topic Appearance: a light or dark background, by the system, or automatically by day and night.
news.voHand: The virtual operator reads your hand better: it judges the gaps between characters and words from the whole over and adapts to your hand during the QSO – even when your gaps are longer, shorter or uneven.
vo.unsureSpace: Unsure gap – the operator read it as a gap between words.
vo.unsureJoin: Unsure gap – the operator read it as a gap between characters (one word).
vo.unsureLegend: (_ / · = unsure gap, read as a gap between words / between characters)
news.voLex: The virtual operator reads the gaps by your hand and by a dictionary: at an unsure gap it picks the reading that makes sense (abbreviations, Q codes, call signs, RST, QSO words). The line “The operator read” shows unsure gaps dotted: _ = read as a gap between words, · = as one word. Wrong characters are still not corrected.
key.hand: Your gaps: between characters ≈ {c}, between words ≈ {w} dots (norm 3 and 7). The evaluation is still against the norm.
news.keyRead: Sending: below the strict reading there is a new line “An operator would read” – the same reading as the virtual operator's (the model of your hand and the lexicon), updated after every pause, no need to send K. Unsure gaps are dotted. It also shows your average gaps between characters and words. The lesson evaluation does not change.
news.keyTempoIn: Opening Sending sets the key to the sending tempo, opening the CW Chat to the receiving tempo (over USB MIDI when switched on). Long pauses no longer confuse the line “An operator would read” – no need to clear the transcript.
